prayerExcerpt.en-US: St. Paschal teaches us never to suffer a day to pass without visiting Jesus in the narrow chamber where He, Whom the heaven itself cannot contain, abides day and night for our sake.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: São Pascoal ensina-nos a nunca deixar passar um dia sem visitar Jesus na estreita morada onde Ele, a quem o próprio céu não pode conter, permanece dia e noite por amor de nós.

meta.face: An Aragonese countryman of about forty-five with a sun-browned olive complexion and a LONG, ANGULAR face — a broad, flat forehead, PROMINENT, BONY cheekbones with shallow hollows under them, DEEP creases from the nose to the corners of the mouth, a LONG, strong, slightly HOOKED nose, deep-set, HEAVY-LIDDED dark eyes under THICK, straight black brows, a WIDE, THIN-LIPPED mouth, a firm chin; black hair cropped short in the Franciscan crown; a thin dark moustache and a small tuft of beard on the chin; the gaze lifted, rapt.
meta.basis: Wikipedia's lead image, an old anonymous canvas inscribed with his name, shows a lay brother in a brown habit, praying with a rosary, with a long, bony face, a strong nose, dark brows and a thin moustache; the card keeps those features. The book tells a shepherd of Aragon, a lay brother of the Franciscans devoted to the Blessed Sacrament, and the angel who showed him the Host while he watched his sheep; its engraving shows a young shepherd kneeling among his flock. Wikipedia: Leo XIII made him patron of Eucharistic congresses and confraternities in 1897, and art gives him the monstrance.
